correctness.rationale: F=(e1,e1,e2), G=(e1,e1+e2,2e1+e2). The first vector is common, and direct enumeration of remaining two binary choices gives positive definite frame operators [[6,3],[3,2]], [[6,2],[2,1]], [[2,1],[1,2]], [[2,0],[0,1]], with determinants 3,2,3,2. Their exact eigenvalues yield positive common lower (7−√41)/2 and upper 4+√13. I independently recomputed the exact 2×2 matrices, determinants, S_F=diag(2,1), S_G=[[6,3],[3,2]] and inverse matrices using SymPy. The canonical dual vectors are F~=(e1/2,e1/2,e2), G~=(2e1/3−e2,−e1/3+e2,e1/3); choosing F~ indices1,2 and G~ index3 gives three collinear e1 vectors, hence loses the frame lower bound. Scalar g-frame identification is exact. If S_F=S_G=S, a shared invertible S^{-1} applied to every original weave preserves uniform bounds.

value.rationale: This concrete counterexample addresses a consequential false blanket stability assertion in weaving frame theory and shows why independently normalizing constituent frames can destroy spanning, even with uniform positive original weaving bounds. The single common-operator sufficient repair identifies the structural issue; it is mathematically motivated beyond a routine frame calculation.

final_claim: Two woven three-vector frames in R² can have canonical dual frame families that are not woven; a specific mixed canonical-dual weave has rank 1. The unconditional canonical-dual preservation stated in Li–Leng–Huang–Li arXiv:1709.05154 Corollary 2.5 is false, while a common frame operator suffices for preservation.
limitations: Demonstrates failure for separately dualized constituents; it does not show all canonical dual weaves fail.
Common constituent frame operator is sufficient but not shown necessary.
No assertion that the uninspected final journal copy repeats the public arXiv corollary verbatim.
